summary: Enclosed L-601 tower with a BC-301 cab on Williams Hill, Monterey County; named for a Cal Fire ranger killed in 1939 and a 1945 fire on the hill; 2019 visit found it serviceable but unstaffed.

facts.design: L-601 enclosed tower, 30 feet tall, with a BC-301 14x14 wood cab and aluminum sheet siding

access.note: The summit is reached by a BLM road that ends at a locked gate, or by a private road Cal Fire may use with the landowner's permission. The Register lists no NHLR sign and no signed directions to the tower.

visit.trail_note: Two dirt roads lead toward the top of Williams Hill. One crosses private land, used with Cal Fire's permission. The BLM road ends at a locked gate at the summit.

facts.agency: Cal Fire (formerly the California Department of Forestry)

events.note: NHLR gives 1942 as the build year and says the cab was constructed that year; Peakbagging's 2010 note gives 1944
Assistant State Forest Ranger Joseph Calandra, the lookout's namesake, was entrapped by the Bixby Mountain Fire near Big Sur on 16 August 1939 and succumbed to his burn injuries
Fire on Williams Hill, 28 July 1945: dozer operator Edward Gates was overtaken by fire; Assistant State Forest Ranger Paul Nesgis was reported missing and his body was found the following March
Date registered on the National Historic Lookout Register: January 12, 2002
Visit by Brad Eells in June 2010: lookout on BLM land, updated with aluminum sheet siding, original outhouse intact, interior reported vandalized
Visit report by Scott McClintock, 4 November 2019: serviceable; needs paint; would need state building inspection and a radiation safety check; not staffed; no NHLR sign posted

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1942 both as the build field and in its description. Peakbagging's 2010 note says the lookout was constructed in 1944. The story uses the Register's 1942 and reports the 1944 figure as the other source's claim. No third source was found.

The Lessons Learned Center places Calandra's death on the Bixby Mountain Fire in Big Sur. A 1939 newspaper item quoted on the California Lookouts site names the Little Sur River. Both point to the same stretch of Monterey County coast, so the story names both.

notes_for_editor: Build year is disputed: NHLR says 1942, Peakbagging's June 2010 note says 1944. Staffing and condition come from the November 2019 NHLR visit report; no newer report was read, so present-day status is unconfirmed. The 30-foot tower height is from Peakbagging and converted to 9.1 m. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced with restricted, based on the 2019 report's locked gate and permission-only private road. The 1945 Gates death is implied by 'overtaken by fire' rather than stated outright; the story says only that he was overtaken. The Lessons page misspells the lookout as 'Casandra'; that spelling is not used. The firelookouthost southern-california table lists Calandra near the word 'Operational', but the text was not clear enough to cite, so it is not used.
